the perfusion-related parameters derived from the IVIM model (D and f) are more accurate than those derived from the DCE-MRI model in predicting the histopathological grade of HNSCC, and that the perfusion parameters derived from the D and f are significantly associated with the histopathological grading of HNSCC.

the perfusion-related parameters of IVIM-DWI are significantly different from those of DCE-MRI and that the perfusion parameters of DCE-MRIs are significantly correlated with IVIM-DWI perfusion parameters.
the perfusion-related intravoxel incoherence motion (IVIM) diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) parameters (D, D*, and f) were significantly higher in head and neck cancer than normal tissue.

the development of a novel method for the determination of the diffusion coefficient of a substance in a porous medium.
the use of diffusion-weighted MRI to characterize the microstructure of normal and diseased tissue.
